title: Hasten to the remembrance
hook: when the call is made on Friday, hasten to remember Allah and leave trade (62:9)

segments.voice: Yesterday, ansar, and your line was be a helper. Did your hand go up somewhere? Today, Surah Al-Jumu'ah, named for Friday. Day six hundred twenty-six.

Friday, a little after noon, in a busy city. A shopkeeper pulls down the shutter halfway and hangs a sign. A taxi driver parks two streets away. Office workers drift out of glass towers in twos and threes, some still on their phones. A boy is running because he's late. They're all heading the same way, toward the sound of the call. For about an hour, buying and selling stops. Surah sixty-two, Al-Jumu'ah, is where that hour comes from.

Verse nine. Pickthall: "O ye who believe! When the call is heard for the prayer of the day of congregation, haste unto remembrance of Allah and leave your trading." The day of congregation is yawm al-jumu'ah, from the root j-m-', to gather. Friday is literally gathering day. The prayer that replaces the noon prayer that day has a sermon, the khutbah, and two units of prayer, prayed together. Now, the verb for hasten is fas'aw. Does that mean run? Commentators said no. Bukhari records that the Prophet ﷺ told people not to rush to the prayer but to walk with calm and dignity, even if they'd miss part of it. So fas'aw means go with intent, set out with purpose, not sprint. And leave your trading is concrete: when the call comes, the deal can wait. Hadith fill in the morning before. Bukhari records that whoever bathes on Friday and goes early to the prayer is like one who offered a camel; a little later, a cow; then a ram, then a hen, then an egg. And when the imam comes out to give the sermon, the angels close their records and sit down to listen. Who is the Friday prayer required of? Most jurists say adult men who are resident and able; women may attend and many do, and for travelers and the sick it's lifted. The verse ends: that is better for you, if you only knew. One hour of the week, cut out of the market, and handed back to remembrance.
screen: `JUMU'AH: GATHERING DAY.` · `FAS'AW: SET OUT WITH PURPOSE.` · `COME EARLY: A CAMEL, THEN AN EGG.` · `THE ANGELS CLOSE THEIR RECORDS.`

segments.voice: The practice: arrive early to something. Sit, and breathe. Think of the next thing you're due at: a prayer, a meeting, a class, a meal with someone. Picture yourself arriving ten minutes early, walking calmly, not rushing. Picture the room before anyone else is there, and you, settled, unhurried, ready to listen. Let your breath slow to that pace now. The bell holds the time.
Khutbah, the sermon that comes with the Friday prayer, when Surah Al-Jumu'ah says to leave trade and hasten to the remembrance of God. Today's word.
Your line: leave trade for a while. Today, arrive early to one thing, and spend the extra minutes simply waiting, phone away. Day six hundred twenty-six.

howItsDone: On Fridays, many Muslims bathe, wear clean clothes, and go to the mosque for the congregational prayer, which has a sermon and two units of prayer in place of the noon prayer; most jurists hold it obligatory for adult, resident men, and women may attend.

fork.setup: the call for the Friday prayer is heard. you're a little late. what does the hadith say to do?
options: run as fast as you can.
skip it and pray at home.
fork.reveal: the Prophet told people not to rush but to walk with calm; hasten in the verse means go with purpose.

original.note: Arabic: so set out for the remembrance of God. sa'y, the root of fas'aw, means effort, going with purpose.

trapdoor: what you thought: a rule to close the shop on Friday.
what it means: one hour of the week cut out of the market and given to remembrance.
what a scholar hears: fas'aw read as purposeful going, not running (cf. Bukhari 636); the 'camel to egg' hadith in Bukhari 881; dhikr Allah here read as the khutbah and prayer.

sources.quoted: O ye who believe! When the call is heard for the prayer of the day of congregation, haste unto remembrance of Allah and leave your trading.
